pr_body:
This commit makes `AnimationBuilder` tree-shakable. When unused, it shaves off around 1400 bytes. 

Developers can now inject `AnimationBuilder` when using `provideAnimationsAsync()`.


fixes #52096

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No
pr_comments:
Yeah, I've thought about that solution too ! 

But there is a dependency issue that makes it non-straightforward : 
`AnimationBuilder` is located in `@angular/animations` while `BrowserAnimationBuilder` should be moved (as proposed) to  `@angular/animations/browser`. 

`@angular/animations/browser` has `@angular/animations` as dependency. So we cannot import the `BrowserAnimationBuilder` and use it in the factory of `AnimationBuilder` (that would introduce a dependency circularity where bazel would complain).   

I've also looked into moving `BrowserAnimationBuilder` to `@angular/animations` but it also has 1 type dependency to `AnimationRenderer` which is located in `@angular/animations/browser`. Hypotheticaly we could move `AnimationBuilder` to `@angular/animations/browser` but this is a breaking change where we could not provide backward compatibility. 

This is why I went with the most straight forward solution : make the `BrowserAnimationBuilder` public and ask developers to directly import/inject it if needed. 

----
Edit: There is another possibility, we can move `BrowserAnimationBuilder` to `@angular/animations` and drop the reference to `@angular/animations/browser` by replacing the imported type `AnimationRenderer` by `Renderer2`. Let me try this.

@JeanMeche I think we should also change commit description to highlight that this refactoring is about making `AnimationBuilder` tree-shakable (the `BrowserAnimationBuilder` reference is no longer relevant, since it remained internal).
@JeanMeche it looks like there is a legit CI failure, could you please take a look when you get a chance? Thank you.
FYI, pushed a rebase, since there was a problem in the main branch at the time of the previous rebase.
I just rebased on main to resolve the conflict following the merge of #52087
@AndrewKushnir Thanks to @devversion's help (cf microsoft/rushstack#4390), the tests are now 🟢 !

comments:
Thank you @zip-fa for logging this. There is still something we need to do about this. 

Currently if you import `BrowserAnimationBuilder` from `@angular/platform-browser/animations` it will effectivily break the code splitting and thus the lazy loading. We cannot import from `@angular/platform-browser/animations` if we want to lazy-load the animations. This is why `provideAnimationsAsync` has been located in a separate entry : `@angular/platform-browser/animations/async`

So there is no way to use AnimationBuilder with async animations for now? Any ETA?
I shaved off my build 175kb today with your async realisation and feeling good about this to be honest
Let me take a look at it so we can hopefully land this for v17.

review_comments: Had to move the `BrowserAnimationBuilder` in the same file as `AnimationBuilder` because of a ` Cannot access 'AnimationBuilder' before initialization` error.

I think we'd need to add a test to see how this would function in case someone injects `AnimationBuilder`, but doesn't enable animations via `provideAnimations` or `provideAnimationsAsync` (which might be even more interesting). This scenario might require an extra handling and potentially an extra check (and logging a good error message to mention that animations was not enabled).
I've introduced a new RuntimeError. What you think of handling it this way ?
